landmarks.name: Kourion
landmarks.writeup: An ancient city-kingdom with well-preserved Greco-Roman ruins including a theater and mosaics.

wiki.extract: Kourion was an important ancient Greek city-state on the southwestern coast of the island of Cyprus. In the twelfth century BCE, after the collapse of the Mycenaean palaces, Greek settlers from Argos arrived on this site.

landmarks.name: Kyrenia Castle
landmarks.writeup: A historic castle located in the harbor of Kyrenia, showcasing Byzantine and Crusader architecture.

wiki.extract: Kyrenia is a city on the northern coast of Cyprus, noted for its historic harbour and castle. It is under the control of Northern Cyprus.

landmarks.name: Tombs of the Kings
landmarks.writeup: A large necropolis dating back to the 4th century BC, known for its underground tombs carved out of solid rock.

wiki.extract: The Tombs of the Kings is a large necropolis about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) north of Paphos harbour in Cyprus. In 1980, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site along with Paphos and Kouklia.

landmarks.name: St. Hilarion Castle
landmarks.writeup: A medieval castle with panoramic views, linked to Crusader legends and fairy tales.

wiki.extract: Saint Hilarion Castle is in the Kyrenia Mountains of Cyprus. This location provided the castle with command of the pass road from Kyrenia to Nicosia. It is the best preserved ruin of the three former strongholds in the Kyrenia mountains, the other two being Kantara and Buffavento.

landmarks.name: Nicosia Old City
landmarks.writeup: The walled city center of the capital, featuring narrow streets, historic buildings, and the Green Line dividing north and south.

wiki.extract: Nicosia, also known as Lefkosia or Lefkoşa, is the capital of Cyprus. It is the southeasternmost capital city among European Union member states. Its northern part is the de facto capital of Northern Cyprus.

cultural_events.name: Carnival
cultural_events.writeup: A lively pre-Lenten festival with parades, costumes, and traditional music celebrated across the island.

wiki.extract: Carnival is a festive season at the close of the Christian pre-Lenten period, consisting of Quinquagesima or Shrove Sunday, Shrove Monday, and Shrove Tuesday or Mardi Gras.

cultural_events.name: Kataklysmos (Festival of the Flood)
cultural_events.writeup: A unique festival celebrating the biblical flood with water-based activities and cultural performances.

wiki.extract: Larnaca, also spelled Larnaka, is a city on the southeast coast of Cyprus and the capital of the Larnaca District. With a district population of 155,000 in 2021, it is the third largest city in the country after Nicosia and Limassol.

cultural_events.name: Wine Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Held in Limassol, this festival celebrates Cyprus's ancient winemaking tradition with tastings and folk music.

wiki.extract: Annual wine festivals celebrate viticulture and usually occur after the harvest of the grapes which, in the northern hemisphere, generally falls at the end of September and runs until well into October or later. They are common in most wine regions around the world and are to be considered in the tradition of other harvest festivals.

cultural_events.name: Anthestiria
cultural_events.writeup: An ancient flower festival marking the arrival of spring with floral decorations and rituals.

wiki.extract: Limassol, also known as Lemesos, is a city on the southern coast of Cyprus. Limassol is the most populated municipality in Cyprus, with a population of 108,105 and is the second-largest urban area in Cyprus, after Nicosia, with an urban population of 198,558. It is the capital of the Limassol District with a population of 262,238.

food_writeup: Cypriot cuisine blends Greek, Turkish, and Middle Eastern influences, featuring dishes like halloumi cheese, souvlaki, meze platters, and fresh seafood, often accompanied by local wines and olive oil.
brief_history: Cyprus has a rich history influenced by various civilizations including the Greeks, Romans, Byzantines, Ottomans, and British. It gained independence from Britain in 1960. The island remains divided between the Greek Cypriot south and Turkish Cypriot north since 1974.

current_conflicts: The island remains divided between the Republic of Cyprus (predominantly Greek Cypriot) and the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, recognized only by Turkey. Ongoing disputes involve territorial control, property rights, and political recognition.

commentary.inflation_management: Euro membership since 2008 means the ECB sets policy; Cyprus tracked the area with sharper swings. It was 0.2% in 2009, -1.5% in 2015 during the bailout-era internal devaluation, and -1.1% in 2020. The 2022 shock pushed it to 8.1%, the series high, but disinflation was fast: 2.3% in 2024 and a projected 0.8% for 2025, one of the lowest in the euro area. The wage-indexation system (COLA) has been a recurring structural debate but did not derail the 2023-24 adjustment.
commentary.debt_management: Cyprus has the most dramatic debt arc in this set: 59% of GDP in 2006, a low of 44.1% in 2008, then the banking crisis and bail-in pushed it to 113.6% in 2020, the series peak, with a second surge during COVID. The turnaround has been equally striking: 80.3% in 2022, projected 55.3% in 2025, driven by strong nominal growth, fiscal surpluses, and repayments. GDP grew from $20.4bn in 2006 to a projected $41.0bn in 2025. Cyprus is the poster child for post-bailout consolidation.

key_events.event: Joined the euro area (January 2008), gaining monetary credibility.
Banking crisis: EU-IMF bailout with the first-ever eurozone deposit bail-in (March 2013); capital controls imposed.
Exited the bailout program on schedule after a sharp but fast adjustment.
COVID-19: debt spiked to 113.6% of GDP, the series peak.
Energy shock inflation of 8.1%; rapid disinflation followed, with 2025 projected at 0.8%.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: Cyprus has earned fiscal credibility through the 2020-25 debt halving, and growth is diversified across tourism, shipping, ICT, and professional services. The risks are external: exposure to regional geopolitical shocks in the Eastern Mediterranean, and a large banking legacy that, while much reduced, still warrants caution. Inflation should remain near the ECB target; the key fiscal task is holding the gains by avoiding procyclical spending as surpluses accumulate.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
